title: Spelling List 8
ruleLine: an r that bends the vowel in front of it into a sound the letters do not promise. Twelve of these thirteen have the blend marked for you; the thirteenth has no r in it at all.

tips.listen: Listen past the letters. There is an r in this word pulling the vowel beside it somewhere else.
tips.boxes: Remember the rule — the vowel next to the r is not saying what it looks like.
tips.reveal: The r-controlled blend is in pink. That is the part the test is looking for.
tips.plain: No r in this one to bend anything. It is the word the teacher chose — spell it the ordinary way.

chart.head: w + or, and it says er
chart.note: the w is what does it. Say or on its own, then put a w in front of it and listen to it change.

chart.head: w + ar, and it says or
chart.note: the same w, bending the other way. Four words this week, and two of them hide the ward at the end.

chart.head: -or on the end, saying er
chart.note: an ending you have met before. It sounds exactly like -er and is not spelled that way.

chart.head: our, saying or
chart.note: three letters for one sound, and the u does no work you can hear.

chart.head: tort, tors = to twist
chart.note: this week's root, and both words carry the same -or-. A sharp answer twists back at you.

chart.head: Find it yourself
chart.note: the teacher's choice. There is no r bending anything here, which is why it is not marked.

words.def: to show deep respect and adoration, especially for a god
words.sent: The little stone church where the village came to ___ had stood on that hill for four hundred years.

words.def: of poorer quality than something else; less good
words.sent: The second storm was ___ than the first, and it took the roof clean off the shed.

words.def: a brave or experienced soldier or fighter
words.sent: Every ___ in the band carried a shield painted with the mark of his own family.

words.def: a tall cupboard where clothes are hung or stored
words.sent: She pushed the coat right to the back of the ___ and shut the door on it.

words.def: a thing given in recognition of service, effort or achievement
words.sent: The farmer offered a small ___ to anyone who could bring the lost dog home.
He walked ___ the light at the far end of the tunnel and never once looked back.

words.def: the imaginary line drawn around the middle of the earth, the same distance from both poles
words.sent: Ships crossing the ___ used to hold a ceremony for anyone making the trip for the first time.

words.def: a cutting tool with two blades fastened in the middle, worked by a thumb and finger
words.sent: He could not find the ___ anywhere, so he tore the paper along the edge of a ruler instead.

words.def: an open area with no roof, shut in by the walls of a large building
words.sent: The hens were let out into the ___ every morning and shut in again at dusk.

words.def: to feel or show deep sorrow for someone who has died
words.sent: The whole village came out to ___ the fisherman who never came back.

words.def: to say something back in a sharp, angry or disrespectful way
words.sent: She did not shout; she only had to ___ once, quietly, and he had nothing left to say.

words.def: to inflict severe pain or suffering on someone
words.sent: No soldier under his command was allowed to ___ a prisoner, whatever the prisoner had done.

words.def: to match or surpass someone, usually by copying the way they do it
words.sent: He hoped one day to ___ his older brother, so he practised the same scales every evening.
